posts.text:
Years of experience is a lagging indicator. Scope is the signal.

I've been reading Indeed Hiring Lab's July report on seniority, and one methodology detail stuck with me more than the headline number.

The headline: in Q1 2026, 69.3% of US software development postings were senior-level. Only 4.5% were entry-level.

The detail: Indeed doesn't classify a posting as senior from its title or the years it asks for. It reads the responsibilities the posting describes.

So the market is literally sorting roles by scope, not tenure.

I think that's the right lens for our own careers too.

"5 years of React, Spring Boot and AWS" describes exposure. It doesn't describe what you were trusted to own: a ticket, a feature, a service, or a system other teams depend on.

The senior signals on public engineering ladders are fairly consistent:

• Decisions you owned, including the ones that turned out wrong
• Work that crossed team boundaries
• Incidents you were accountable for, not just paged into
• Engineers who got better because you were around
• Designs you wrote down before you built them

The last one is underrated. Plenty of engineers do real design work and never leave an artifact. If the reasoning only lives in a Slack thread, nobody can see the scope, including your next hiring manager.

AI makes this sharper, not softer. When producing code gets cheap, what's left to evaluate is judgment: what to build, what not to build, and how you'd know the output is right.

So the question I'm asking myself isn't "how many years do I have?"

It's "what's the largest thing I'd be trusted to own tomorrow, and where's the evidence?"

For those who hire: what's the clearest scope signal you look for that candidates rarely show?

#SoftwareEngineering #CareerGrowth #SystemDesign

posts.text:
🧱 From Boxes to Building Blocks 🧱

I've worked in software engineering, program management, business development, consulting, and IT recruitment. Looking back, tech was easier to sort into boxes. 📦 Software, hardware, and infrastructure mostly sat in the customer's own data center. It wasn't easy, but it was clear who owned what.

Then things shifted. Microsoft's "Software Plus Services" push, and later hybrid cloud, let companies keep some things in house and hand others to outside providers. What I first saw as fragmentation, I now see as specialization. 


🔍 Specialization Is Showing Up Everywhere 🔍

We build differently now, too. Tools like React help developers organize big, complex apps. Splitting applications into services creates clearer boundaries, though the complexity just moves into the connections between the pieces. 


🎓 Certifications Got More Specific 🎓

Certifications followed the same path. Labels like Java, Oracle, and PeopleSoft once covered a lot of ground. Today, Microsoft has moved from MCSA, MCSD, and MCSE to role based certifications, and Kubernetes has separate credentials for administration, development, and security. Expertise is now described in smaller, more precise pieces. 


💡 Why Certifications Still Matter Now 💡

When job requirements get specific, employers want clearer evidence of what someone knows. In the Linux Foundation's 2025 State of Tech Talent survey, 71% of organizations said certifications are important when evaluating technical skills. Hands on experience and portfolios ranked even higher, so think of a certification as a solid starting point, not the whole story. 


🤝 A Win for Recruiters 🤝

From my recruiting days, I can tell you this helps recruiters, too. "Cloud engineer" only tells you so much. A relevant certification helps a recruiter ask sharper screening questions, compare candidates to what the hiring manager needs, and spot where more assessment is needed. Just know what each credential covers, since a foundational cert and an implementation focused cert aren't the same. It's about matching evidence to the work, not counting badges. 


🏁 Make Your Skills Easy to Recognize 🏁

A certification won't erase onboarding, since knowing a platform isn't the same as knowing a company's systems and team habits. Even AWS says there's "no true substitute for experience." Still, a relevant cert plus recent project work can shorten the road to contributing. 🚀 

In a tough job market, pick certifications that fit the work you want, pair them with real examples of what you've built or improved, and share that story with confidence. 🙌 

Certifications give employers a clearer starting point and a credible case that you can do the work. ✨

Think about where this started.

A decision made with more hope than certainty. A first client that felt like a miracle. The early months of figuring everything out as you went. The nights you were not sure it was going to work, followed by the mornings you showed up anyway.

You built something from nothing. That is not a small thing.

But here is what often gets lost in the middle of building.

The same determination that got the business started can become the thing that keeps it from growing. Because effort alone, sustained indefinitely, without a clear financial picture, creates a ceiling. You can work harder and harder and still not break through it. Not because something is wrong with you, but because the business has outgrown the systems it started with.

At some point, working more is not the answer. Working with better information is.

When you can see your real profit margin, you can price with confidence. When you understand your cash flow, you can plan instead of react. When your financial picture is clear, you can make decisions about growth, hiring, and investment that are based on reality rather than instinct.

You have already done the hard part. You built it.

posts.text:
AI can write the code.
A good software engineer still has to know whether it should ship.
I use AI every day as a frontend developer.
It helps me learn faster and improve the way I work.
The judgment about what reaches production still stays with me.
𝟭. 𝗜𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗹𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿?
Subscriptions, API usage, infrastructure, maintenance, and review time belong in the same calculation as hiring.
The leverage is real.
A lower total cost still has to be proven.
𝟮. 𝗪𝗵𝗼 𝗼𝘄𝗻𝘀 𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘂𝗿𝗲?
When I ship incorrect code, my team investigates and owns the fix.
When AI generates that code and I merge it, responsibility stays with:
• The person who reviewed it
• The team that released it
• The company that set the process
The provider supplies the tool.
Shipping remains a human decision.
𝟯. 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗮 𝗱𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲?
Over the next five years, companies will look for engineers who can frame a problem, choose an architecture, review generated code, protect security, and maintain what they ship.
𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗜 𝗮𝗺 𝗳𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴
• Fundamentals: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and the browser
• Problem framing and architecture
• Code review, debugging, and testing
• Security and product judgment
• Clear communication with design, product, and engineering
I plan to keep building these skills, use AI to learn faster, and understand every generated change before it reaches users.
I would like to hear your thoughts in the comments.
I respect your time, and I value every comment.

𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄
1. Has AI reduced your overall cost of software development?
2. Who should be accountable when AI-generated code causes a production issue?
3. Which skills are you focusing on to stay valuable over the next five years?

Recruiter: "So, do you know C?"

Me: "Yeah. I've been writing embedded C for about five years now."

Recruiter: "Great. And have you worked with React?"

Me: "..."

That little silence said a lot.

Look, I get it, recruiters juggle a hundred roles a day. But embedded hiring has this funny problem where the job and the interview sometimes feel like they're for two completely different roles.

The job is: bring up a board that's never booted before, chase a bug that shows up once a week and never the same way twice, make a CAN network behave, write a bootloader that must never brick a module.

The interview is: reverse a linked list on a whiteboard.

I'm not saying DSA doesn't matter. It does. But if you're hiring someone to debug real hardware, maybe ask them about the last board that didn't boot.

Embedded folks, what's the strangest question you've been asked in an interview for an embedded role?

posts.text:
We applaud recent graduates for taking time off to explore and reset. But when seasoned professionals step back for a year, we often react with skepticism instead of support. Why is that?

An employment gap isn’t a red flag—It can be a sign of strength.

It’s time to rethink how we view employment gaps when considering candidates.
Somehow, we’ve come to expect careers to run in a straight, unbroken line. When someone has a gap on their resume, the questions start: Why did they step away? What were they doing? Why weren’t they working?

But perhaps we're asking the wrong questions.

What if that gap shows someone recognized they were burned out or just needed a break to recharge? What if they made a conscious choice to focus on their mental health and well-being after decades of hard work?

That’s not weakness. If anything, it takes real strength.

We support young people who travel, try new things, and take time off before starting the next chapter. We know there’s value in stepping away for perspective.

So why don’t we offer the same understanding to experienced professionals?

Why judge someone who’s spent years working hard for taking some time for themselves?
Career breaks aren’t always about struggling to find work. Sometimes, they’re a thoughtful, planned choice—earned after years of effort.

Let’s be honest: it takes guts to realize you need a break and actually take one.

We say mental health and work-life balance matter. But when someone steps away to protect their well-being, they often face judgment when they return to work.

That doesn’t add up.

If you’re hiring, look past the dates on a resume.

A gap doesn’t mean someone lacks ambition or work ethic. It doesn’t erase years of experience or everything they bring to the table.

Instead of focusing on the gap, look at the whole person—their skills, experience, and what they offer now.

Careers are marathons, not sprints. Sometimes, a break is exactly what someone needs to come back stronger and more energized.

Let's stop treating employment gaps like red flags. People are more than the dates on their resume.

Taking a career break doesn’t mean you’ve lost your drive. Sometimes, it’s just realizing your well-being matters too.

That should never be held against anyone.

posts.text:
We moved millions of records from MySQL to PostgreSQL while 700,000 people kept using the system. Nobody noticed. And data now loads 3x faster. 🚀

It was a nationwide training center platform in Iraq, used every day, so shutting it down for a weekend wasn’t an option.

We didn’t just copy the tables over. We redesigned the schema along the way. Same data, better structure, and that alone made reads 3x faster.

How we did it without downtime:
 - Tested our backups first, by actually restoring them
 - Kept MySQL running and added Postgres next to it
 - Sent every new write to both databases
 - Moved old data in small batches with checkpoints, so a failed batch just re-ran on its own
 - Compared both databases, then moved reads to Postgres bit by bit
 - Kept MySQL live until the very end, just in case

✅ Zero downtime
✅ Zero data lost
⚡ 3x faster reads

Biggest lesson for me: a good migration is boring. Lots of small steps you can undo, no big dramatic switch.

I’m a full-stack engineer in Dubai (Node.js, NestJS, React) and I’m open to new roles. Happy to chat if you’re hiring. 👋

Ever read a job description and still have no idea what the company is actually looking for?

The job title says Frontend Developer.

But the requirements include:

React and Next.js

Backend API development

Database management

Cloud infrastructure

DevOps

UI/UX design

At some point, you start wondering:

Are they hiring a frontend developer or expecting one person to handle the entire engineering team?

This is something job seekers should pay attention to.

Before applying, look beyond the job title.

Check:

What will you actually be responsible for?
Which skills are essential, and which are just nice to have?
Does the experience level match the responsibilities?

Is the role clearly explained?

A long list of technologies doesn't automatically mean it's a good opportunity.

And sometimes, the biggest problem isn't your resume. It's understanding what the employer really expects.

My wellness chatbot used to repeat itself. Here’s how I rebuilt it.
Rowl AI is a mental wellness app I built and deployed. Version 1 worked, but Sera, its chatbot, had real problems: it ran on a retired model, it fetched the oldest messages instead of the newest, and refreshing the page wiped the conversation.
So I rebuilt the core for Rowl AI 2.0:
🧠 Three layers of memory: recent messages, a short long-term summary, and the user’s profile with their latest journal mood
🔁 A three-model failover chain on Groq, so one dead model no longer breaks the chat
🛟 A crisis safeguard on both client and server: a persistent support banner with one-tap helpline buttons, a calming grounding screen (breathing voice, soft tones, a haptic pulse), and an optional alert email to a trusted contact
👩‍⚕️ A doctor dashboard with an AI-written pre-session brief
🔐 Password recovery with a 6-digit OTP
☁️ Graceful fallback when the database is unreachable
The biggest lesson: the unglamorous parts matter most. Failure handling, safe defaults, and what happens when something breaks at 2am are what make an app feel trustworthy.
Rowl is a self-care tool, not a substitute for professional help.
Built with React, Node/Express, MongoDB, Groq and Razorpay. I build with AI-assisted tools, and I’m making sure I can explain every layer.

posts.text:
The Miracle Morning:  Why Great Entrepreneurs Rush Slowly

The Reactive Trap

Most entrepreneurs start the day already behind. The phone lights up before the coffee does, an overnight email from a client, a cash-flow question from the bookkeeper, a team member who needs an answer now. Within minutes, we react instead of leading.

The Magic Morning

The most effective founders I work with protect what I call the "magic morning". The first 20 to 30 minutes of the day, before the world gets a vote. For many of them, the anchor is meditation.

Rush, Slowly

The Romans had a phrase for it. Festina lente, "make haste slowly." It sounds like a contradiction until you have run a business.  

MIT’s & MIG’s 
 
Old school, gain clarity on the Most Important Tasks and Most Important Goals that need to get done by simply jotting them down. Sure feels good checking them off, completing the day with that piece of paper in the trash can, ready for a fresh start tomorrow.

Power Down to Power Up

Think of your morning practice as powering down before the day powers up. Like a captain checking the instruments before leaving port, you are confirming your heading before the weather hits. 

You don't know what is coming to you today. A lost deal, a hiring crisis, an unexpected opportunity. You can decide who will be standing there when it arrives.

Then open the inbox. The day will still rush. You will just be the one setting the pace. 

#Pacing #Cadence #Clarity

posts.text:
He graduated from Princeton with perfect grades.

But his interviewer wasn’t impressed.

In the movie The Reluctant Fundamentalist (2012), Changez Khan interviews for a highly competitive financial analyst position at Underwood Samson.

He proudly explains that he’s never received a B and is about to graduate summa cum laude.

The interviewer, Jim Cross, barely reacts.

He’s already heard similar answers from several candidates that day.

Instead, Jim starts asking about Changez’s background, his financial struggles, and what motivates him.

Then comes the moment that changes the conversation.

Changez confidently tells him:

“Whether or not you hire me, Jim, I am going to win.”

The interviewer finally smiles.

What makes this scene interesting is the distinction between qualifications and motivation.

Academic achievements demonstrate discipline, intelligence, and consistency.

But they don’t necessarily reveal how someone responds to setbacks, handles uncertainty, or pursues difficult goals.

Great hiring decisions require understanding what candidates have accomplished and what drives them to accomplish more.

The strongest candidates bring more than impressive credentials.

They bring the determination to turn their potential into results.

#Leadership #Hiring #CareerDevelopment

posts.text:
261108 – Recently, a client complained to a coach, that the recruiter the client spoke to, was too abrasive. When I heard such a comment, I wondered to myself, “What is the purpose of the comment?”

Firstly, as job-seekers, our objective is to get the job. What we think of the recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, or human recource personnels, is not important. Focus on what we need to do. We do not have to decide to turn down the offer, because we do not have the offer. We can withdraw our application, but have we assessed the opportunity thoroughly enough?

Secondly, when we watch the news, we focus on the news. We do not complain that the newscaster is being too negative. He/She is just reporting the news. We can choose not to watch the news when there is too much negativity. But for our job-hunt, we cannot afford to tune away, but only regulate ourselves accordingly.

In fact, we need to be conscious, are we emotionally affected by the news, or are we just unwilling to accept the truth? We can turn away temporarily. But to get to our goal, accepting the truth, and finding ways around it, is necessary.

Lastly, everything that we encounter is neutral. Positive or negative, is how we frame it. And in whatever that we do, focus on what we are trying to achieve, rather than being distracted by things around us. How we accept the things that we face, can help us to grow, developed our character, and make us better and stronger.

"Life is 10% what happens to you and 90% how you react to it." The successful candidate who got the job, the colleague who got rewarded with a bonus and promotion, the pleasant service provider who got a superb review, the thriving business owner, they have their share of encounters with rude, nasty, abrasive, or even unreasonable individuals in their courses towards their goals. But they still thrive.

Do what is necessary, to get to where we want to be. There will be noises along the way. Tuning in to them, or shutting them off, is up to us. Our objective is to get to our goal, no matter what it takes.


=> we have an objective and a goal
=> there will be distractions around us
=> "Life is 10% what happens to you and 90% how you react to it"
=> focus on our goal, and get to it, no matter what it takes

posts.text:
Every missed call is a patient who books with the next clinic. 📞 
So I built an AI receptionist for dental clinics, and it’s live. 😍 

It answers the phone in a natural voice, checks opening hours, and takes the booking request. The clinic’s staff then see the full transcript and a call summary in a private dashboard.
In the demo call, the caller asks for 12 AM. The assistant says the clinic is closed and offers 12 PM instead. The booking request lands on the schedule.
What’s under the hood:

→ Voice layer: Vapi (the call, speech and turn-taking)
→ Backend: Fastify + TypeScript, inputs validated with zod, webhook protected by a shared secret
→ Booking logic: opening hours, visit lengths and lead time in tested functions; Postgres advisory lock so two callers can’t take the same slot
→ Dashboard: Next.js 15 + React 19, signed-cookie login
→ Public demo reads a masked feed only: no phone numbers, no transcripts.

The clinic is fictional, but the build is real and you can try it yourself.
I’m a Senior Full Stack Engineer (React, Next.js, Node.js, TypeScript, Python, Postgres, AWS) with 5+ years of experience. I’m open to remote contract roles, and I build AI assistants and web apps for small businesses.

If you’re hiring, or you run a clinic or service business that loses calls, send me a message.

posts.text:
261108 – Recently, a client complained to a coach, that the recruiter the client spoke to, was too abrasive.  When I heard such a comment, I wondered to myself, “What is the purpose of the comment?”
 
Firstly, as job-seekers, our objective is to get the job.  What we think of the recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, or human recource personnels, is not important.  Focus on what we need to do.  We do not have to decide to turn down the offer, because we do not have the offer.  We can withdraw our application, but have we assessed the opportunity thoroughly enough?
 
Secondly, when we watch the news, we focus on the news.  We do not complain that the newscaster is being too negative.  He/She is just reporting the news.  We can choose not to watch the news when there is too much negativity.  But for our job-hunt, we cannot afford to tune away, but only regulate ourselves accordingly.
 
In fact, we need to be conscious, are we emotionally affected by the news, or are we just unwilling to accept the truth?  We can turn away temporarily.  But to get to our goal, accepting the truth, and finding ways around it, is necessary.
 
Lastly, everything that we encounter is neutral.  Positive or negative, is how we frame it.  And in whatever that we do, focus on what we are trying to achieve, rather than being distracted by things around us.  How we accept the things that we face, can help us to grow, developed our character, and make us better and stronger.
 
"Life is 10% what happens to you and 90% how you react to it."  The successful candidate who got the job, the colleague who got rewarded with a bonus and promotion, the pleasant service provider who got a superb review, the thriving business owner, they have their share of encounters with rude, nasty, abrasive, or even unreasonable individuals in their courses towards their goals.  But they still thrive.
 
Do what is necessary, to get to where we want to be.  There will be noises along the way.  Tuning in to them, or shutting them off, is up to us.  Our objective is to get to our goal, no matter what it takes.
 
 
=> we have an objective and a goal
=> there will be distractions around us
=> "Life is 10% what happens to you and 90% how you react to it"
=> focus on our goal, and get to it, no matter what it takes

posts.text:
99 cold emails in one inbox. 1 reply.

Watch the counter in the video.
It's one prospect's Monday morning.
(An illustration, but you've seen this inbox.)

99 emails say the same thing:
"Quick question about your growth."
Same tools. Same AI. Same template.

1 email says something else:
"Saw the hiring post for your new location. One idea for week one."

That's the one that got: "Good timing. Thursday?"

The difference isn't the writing.
It's knowing what just changed for them.

Doing that by hand takes hours a day.
So I built an AI system that does it for me:

1. Every morning it checks for signals
Job posts, funding rounds, new leaders, CRM switches.

2. AI checks each company against my ideal client
No fit, no email.

3. It writes one first line about what changed
Not "quick question". Not about me.

4. Replies land in my CRM with the signal attached
So I know why they answered before I open the email.

I still read every email before it goes out.
The system does the digging. I do the deciding.

Changing what I react to has moved my reply rates more than any copy tweak ever did.

The tools got cheaper.
Standing out didn't.

Comment SIGNAL and I'll show you how the system works.

posts.text:
Working in VA law enforcement gives us the privilege of serving a community that has already given so much.

Let’s face it, many of our Veterans have strong, Type A personalities. They’re direct, outspoken, independent, and not always interested in being told what to do. Some are dealing with pain, frustration, mental health challenges, or simply having a bad day. As VAP we’re going to be on the receiving end of that frustration.

Our job isn’t to win an argument. It’s to handle the situation professionally. Not every raised voice is a threat, not every disagreement is disrespect, and not every challenge to our authority requires a reaction.

When we allow our emotions to dictate our response, we risk escalating the situation, making the job harder for fellow officers and medical staff, and damaging the trust our community places in us. You can be firm without being disrespectful, assertive without being aggressive, and authoritative without being arrogant.

Professionalism doesn’t mean being a pushover. It means having the discipline, judgment, and emotional intelligence to know the difference between a genuine threat and someone who’s simply frustrated. We chose this profession, and with that comes a responsibility to uphold a higher standard, regardless of how others treat us.

Our Veterans don’t have to be easy to deal with to deserve dignity and professionalism.
Sometimes the greatest demonstration of authority is knowing when not to react.

Be firm. Be fair. Be accountable. Remember who we serve.

posts.text:
Junior devs, your LinkedIn headline is quietly costing you work.

"Full-stack web developer. HTML, CSS, JS, React, WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, Python..."

You think that reads as versatile.
To the person hiring, it reads as "still figuring it out."

Here's the uncomfortable truth:
Nobody searches for a generalist.
They search for "fix my WooCommerce checkout."
"Move my site to Webflow CMS."
"Why is my Shopify store so slow?"

So pick one lane. Own it for 12 months.
Build three portfolio pieces that solve that exact problem.
Write about it here every single week.

It will feel like you're shrinking your options.
In reality, it's the moment people can finally find you.

Specialists get referred. Generalists get compared on price.

You can always widen later. Standing out on day one in a crowd of "I do everything" is the hard part.

If you had to pick ONE niche today, what would it be?

posts.text:
So, what does it actually take to become an AI Engineer in 2026?

I'm not sure. Competition is growing, and so is demand. But one thing is clear: #AIengineering skills are becoming increasingly valuable, even outside traditionally technical roles.

As I was learning AI engineering skills myself, I wanted to know what the market actually needs, rather than just follow online learning roadmaps.

So I analysed the latest 1,488 AI Engineer job postings (with comparison to 6,160 SWE roles) across #Switzerland, #Germany, the #Netherlands and other European markets (July–November 2026). ( P.S. This was made possible by Jobfish.ing, a platform we've been building to help #jobhunters apply for the right opportunities in the fastest way. )

Three questions I want to answer for myself:
1. What skills are employers looking for in AI Engineers?
2. How do these differ from traditional Software Engineers?
3. Which industries are hiring AI Engineers?

Some takeaways:

1. LLMs are becoming standard. Python (75%), LLMs (69%), AI Agents (51%) and RAG (49%) are the most frequently mentioned skills. Around 80% of roles focus on building AI applications, while only ~12% involve model training or research. In other words, think software engineering with an LLM stack.

2. AI Engineer and SWE roles have distinct skill profiles:

More common in AI roles: LLMs, RAG, Python, AI Agents and Machine Learning.
Shared by both: Architecture/system design, CI/CD, security and privacy.
More common in SWE roles: Java, React, SQL databases, clean code/design patterns and Agile/Scrum.

I've included the full analysis in the pictures.

Curious to hear: What AI engineering skills are you prioritising in 2026?

🚨 Hiring is broken, but the best startups are quietly fixing it.  

A few years ago, recruiters would CTRL+F for keywords—"React, 5+ YOE, AWS"—and call it a day. Now? The best teams don’t care about your resume bullets. They care about what you’ve *built* and how you solve real problems.  

Forward-deployed engineers, proof-of-work projects, and take-home challenges that mirror actual work are replacing leetcode hazing. The shift is simple: **Can you do the job, not just interview for it?**

posts.text:
A REQUEST TO RECRUITERS & HR PROFESSIONALS 🙏

Dear Recruiters, HR Professionals and Hiring Managers,

Please understand the feelings of job seekers.

When you publish a job vacancy on LinkedIn, many people react, comment and show interest. Some candidates politely comment, "Please share your resume."

Job seekers trust your words, prepare their CVs and send their resumes with hope of getting an opportunity.

But unfortunately, after receiving the resume, many recruiters don't respond. No interview call, no rejection message, not even a simple update.

Please remember:

- A job seeker's time is valuable.
- Every resume represents someone's hope and hard work.
- Not every candidate will be selected, and that's absolutely fine.
- But a simple response can make a big difference.
- If a candidate is not suitable, please communicate it politely.

You don't have to give everyone a job, but you can give everyone a response.

Behind every resume, there is a person waiting for an opportunity, someone working hard to support their family and build a better future.

Respect job seekers. Respect their time. Respect their hopes.

Let's make LinkedIn a platform for genuine opportunities, not just collecting resumes.

posts.text:
I built my own Vercel from scratch. 🚀
You sign in with GitHub, pick a Vite/React repo, and the platform builds it in an isolated AWS Fargate container. Build logs stream live to your browser, and the site goes live at <slug>.yourdomain.com. A git push redeploys it automatically.
Under the hood it’s 10 backend services in a TypeScript monorepo, using Express, Postgres, Redis, BullMQ, Kafka, ClickHouse, S3 and Socket.IO. These were the parts that taught me the most:
🔒 One active build per user. A Redis lock stores the owning deployment ID and is released with a Lua compare-and-delete. A late cancel can never free a lock that now belongs to someone else. Postgres compare-and-set updates mean a cancelled deploy can never flip back to “ready”.
📡 Live logs with no gaps or duplicates. Container → Kafka → two consumer groups. One fans out over Socket.IO and the other persists to ClickHouse. Every event carries a per-deployment sequence number. The browser subscribes first, then fetches history, then merges by sequence.
🔑 Auth that assumes tokens get stolen. Refresh tokens rotate on every use. If an old one is replayed, an atomic Lua script detects it and revokes the whole session.
🛡️ Safer builds. User code runs with a minimal environment, so platform secrets are never visible to it. Secrets are redacted from every log line, including URL-encoded and base64 forms.
The biggest lesson: the happy path is the easy part. The real design work is in cancellations, crashes, retries, duplicate webhooks and Kafka outages.
I’m a final-year B.Tech student looking for Software Engineer roles in India. If you’re hiring, or just want to talk distributed systems, I’d love to connect.

posts.text:
New here, or been reading all week? One post about working with me — then back to the useful stuff.

I am Muhammad Hamad, a Full Stack Developer and AI Engineer with 8 years of experience, working remotely with clients and teams worldwide.

Most good projects I have seen do not start with "build us an AI system". They start with one workflow that wastes a team's week.

So here is how working with me usually starts:

1. You describe the workflow that wastes your team's time — leads, data entry, follow-ups, documents, support.
2. I tell you honestly whether AI, automation, or simple software is the right fix — including when the answer is "do not build anything yet".
3. We start narrow: one task, clear rules, a human checking the important steps. Then we expand only if it works.

What I build around that first step: workflow automation, AI features and agents with rules and limits you control, and the software around them — SaaS platforms, dashboards, and internal tools.

My stack: Python, TypeScript, React, Next.js, NestJS, FastAPI — plus OpenAI and Claude APIs, LangChain, and retrieval systems.

Two ways to start a conversation:
- Businesses: message me the workflow. I will reply with the first step I would take.
- Recruiters and hiring managers: message me the role. My portfolio and experience are at hamadshafiq.com.

No pressure, no pitch beyond this post. Tomorrow we go back to teaching.

Which workflow would you bring to that first conversation?

posts.text:
Target 3,49jt lapangan kerja baru di 2027, tapi porsi kerja formalnya cuman 40%-an.

Artinya hampir 60% pekerja kita masih di sektor informal. Sedihnya, sekarang banyak banget talent berkualitas yang malah kerja informal. No disrespect, but it’s a shame.

Good thing now some of them have a chance. Through EOR, senior engineer atau marketer di Indonesia bisa digaji perusahaan luar pakai standar gaji di sana, sambil tetap kerja dari Indo dengan gaji dollar (klise, I know).

I don’t believe in work family, but I do believe friendship outside of work exists. And in this economy, fair2an aja kalau ada yang ambil a better opportunity.

Jadi saingan lu buat dapetin senior talent sekarang termasuk perusahaan luar.

Buat local founders dan C-level yang lagi nyusun headcount plan 2027, tiga hal yang perlu dibenerin dari sekarang:
1. Benchmark gaji role senior lu ke market yang sebenarnya, termasuk offer remote dari luar.
2. Tulis policy flexibility yang jelas di offer letter, jangan cuma janji pas interview.
3. Kasih career path dan struktur management yang kelihatan dari hari pertama.

posts.text:
What an incredible 3 days in Bali! 🌴

I recently participated in the "Solve and Innovate with Emerging Technologies" workshop organized by BRI Corporate University.

The energy was unmatched! We had 28 participants split into groups, all focused on applying the Challenge Based Learning (CBL) framework to fresh product ideas or enhancement. A massive shoutout to our stellar mentors who guided us through the grind: Kusuma S., I Putu Dana Putra, and Reva Prasetya.

Fun fact: I had just chatted with Kusuma S. a few days prior about the iOS developer community in Bali, Swift Bali. This world is indeed a small world! 😅.

Returning to the CBL framework felt like a beautiful trip down memory lane. This is the exact framework used by the Apple Developer Academy, where I first mastered it back in 2018 as a learner in the very first cohort. It truly brought back some of the best memories of my journey.

For those unfamiliar, CBL breaks down into 3 core phases:
1. Engage: Moving from a broad "Big Idea" to a sharp "Essential Question," which ultimately shapes an actionable "Challenge."
2. Investigate: Mapping out guiding questions and conducting deep-dive research to fully understand the user's core pain points.
3. Act: Designing, building, and deploying a prototype, followed by rigorous user testing and continuous iterations.

The result of our sprint? We successfully re-engineered a user journey in our application, transforming a rigid 8-step process into 8 flexible ways to transact. By fully exploiting native iPhone capabilities, we turned complex workflows into a seamless, effortless User Experience.

What exactly did we cook up? You will just have to wait for our upcoming app release! 😉.

To top off the workshop, we were invited to visit the Apple Developer Academy @ BINUS, Bali, which stands out as the only academy in Indonesia that opens its doors to international learners.

It was awesome to catch up with my former mentor, Handy Tanuhardja, and connect with the Head of Academy, Joe Sibayan, alongside other brilliant mentors. While our time was short due to our packed schedule with the BRI team, this visit was incredibly meaningful. It is bound to open doors for exciting future transformations at PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk.

#LifeAtBRI #AppleDeveloperAcademy #ChallengeBasedLearning #iOSDeveloper #FintechInnovation #UserExperience #ProductDesign

Thailand's Data Centres Will Soon Have to Pitch for Power

Thailand's data centres will soon have to compete for electricity and water under a new draft framework, pitching for access based on what they contribute to the economy. The draft sets seven tiers by power demand from 0.5MW to over 200MW, designates data centres a national priority sector, and is expected to reopen new applications in early 2027 — raising the question of whether the process will attract better investment or push operators toward Malaysia and Indonesia.

Here's what we know:
· New projects must pitch for power, water and incentives

Quality rarely drops all at once.

More often, it drifts.

A standard is clear at the beginning.

Then the programme tightens.

More contractors come onto site.

Different supervisors take over areas.

Small exceptions get accepted.

Temporary fixes stay in place.

Inspection discipline becomes less consistent.

And slowly, the standard that everyone started with is no longer the standard being delivered everywhere.

That is what makes quality drift difficult to spot.

Nothing looks dramatically wrong.

But over time, variation starts to appear between:

• Contractors
• Work packages
• Areas
• Shifts
• Supervisors
• Stages of completion

On data-centre and critical infrastructure projects, that inconsistency can create real problems later during testing, commissioning and handover.

Dedicated QA/QC helps keep the original standard visible throughout the project.

Not only by identifying defects, but by asking:

Are we still building to the same standard we agreed at the start?

At Assured Technical Services, we support developers and project teams with independent inspections, quality oversight, documentation review, defect management, commissioning support and close-out verification.

The objective is simple:

posts.text:
Adaptation finance is not held back by willingness, but by the conditions that shape investment decisions.

That is the argument of a new Climate Bonds Initiative report, summarised in a blog on 30 September 2026. Climate-related disaster exposure has increased by 80% since 2005, and emerging markets and developing economies alone face annual adaptation and resilience (A&R) investment needs of USD310-365bn by 2035. Those needs already dwarf public capabilities. Yet resilience finance remains less developed than mitigation finance, with greater clarity still needed on what counts as a credible resilience investment.

Private sector adaptation finance sits at around USD5bn a year, and Climate Bonds argues policymakers have the potential to scale it to USD50bn a year.

The report, "Financing Climate Adaptation and Resilience: Ten Policy Approaches", collects ten examples of what governments and public institutions already do.

The first is embedding resilience in decision-making, from national adaptation planning to climate-related disclosure. Indonesia's National Adaptation Plan is cited as a whole-of-government approach linking adaptation priorities to development planning and public finance.

The second is making resilience worth investing in, and this is where the built environment appears directly. Singapore's incentive scheme for green buildings grants additional floor area to developments that meet environmental targets, creating economic value for developers without direct public expenditure. As fiscal space tightens, Climate Bonds expects such fiscally efficient policies to matter more.

The third is closing risk protection gaps, where insurance, contingent finance and other risk-transfer mechanisms step in. Protection gaps are not confined to developing economies: significant climate risks remain uninsured in developed markets.

No single instrument clears the barriers. Scaling resilience finance will need a combination of approaches, stronger institutional capacity, better climate risk data and collaboration across governments, development finance institutions, regulators, insurers and investors.

Source: Climate Bonds Initiative, "Financing climate adaptation and resilience: ten policy approaches", 30 September 2026

posts.text:
A Bangkok condominium, a Phnom Penh apartment and a Bali villa may have similar asking prices and advertised rental yields, yet offer very different ownership rights and resale options.

An overlooked detail: a foreign ownership quota does not necessarily count apartments.

THAILAND
Eligible foreigners can own condominium units up to 49% of the registered building’s total unit floor area. A quota certificate and evidence of qualifying funds matter at transfer. The limit does not mean 49 of every 100 apartments are available.

CAMBODIA
Under the 2010 law and Sub-Decree 82, eligible foreigners can own private units above ground level in co-owned buildings, up to 70% of the total private-unit floor area. Strata title to a unit is not land ownership.

INDONESIA
Bali property cannot be reduced to a single “leasehold versus freehold” choice. Hak Pakai (right to use), apartment strata rights, underlying land title, buyer eligibility and location conditions affect what can be transferred. A villa and an apartment unit require different due diligence.

Here is a simple test of why the quota definition matters.
Imagine 100 hypothetical units: 50 of 35 m² and 50 of 85 m². Total floor area: 6,000 m².
• A 49% area ceiling equals 2,940 m².
• Forty-nine 85 m² units total 4,165 m² — above that ceiling.
• Forty-nine 35 m² units total 1,715 m² — below it.
Same unit count, different outcome. This does not establish quota availability in a real building.

Price per square metre has its own denominator problem. In a hypothetical listing, a $180,000 apartment advertised as 60 m² costs $3,000/m². If only 48 m² is usable interior space, the price is $3,750/m² on that basis — 25% higher. Neither figure is automatically false; the definitions answer different questions. Cross-market comparisons need consistent floor-area measurements.

Yield comparisons have a similar flaw.
Consider a hypothetical $150,000 property at $1,100 monthly rent: 8.8% gross yield. With ten rented months, 15% management fees and $2,300 in annual expenses and reserves, it generates $7,050 — a 4.7% operating yield before financing, tax and transaction costs.
Gross yield, net yield and cash-on-cash return measure different things.
At NovAsia Estate, we begin with three questions: What property right can be registered? What cash flow remains after ownership costs? And how liquid could the asset be at resale? A brochure alone cannot answer them.

Due diligence also needs to address developer history, off-plan contracts, rental rules, management fees and resale liquidity. Asking prices are not sale prices.
This is a comparison of published rules and illustrative calculations, not a survey of completed sales, actual rental occupancy or investor returns.
Sources: Thailand Department of Lands; Cambodia’s 2010 foreign-ownership law and Sub-Decree 82; Indonesia’s Regulation 18/2021; UNCTAD.

Following my recent visit to Indonesia, having been involved in setting up a number of schools in the country over the years, I have been considering the opportunities for international education in a country whose scale makes it difficult to ignore, but is as yet relatively under exploited by independent U.K. schools. 

An August 2025 overview by investment adviser BDA Partners estimated that Indonesia had a population of approximately 278 million, including around 71 million people aged 5–19. It identified approximately 180 international K–12 school brands and 80,000 enrolments.

The report distinguishes premium schools charging more than US$20,000 annually, mass-affluent schools charging US$10,000–20,000, and value-tier schools charging less than US$10,000.

These are estimates from 2025, rather than a verified 2026 census, but they illustrate the diversity of the market.

There is, however, an important issue beyond population and purchasing power: the operating and investment structure.

Indonesia’s foreign-curriculum schools operate within a regulatory framework involving cooperation education units and local foundations. The precise legal structure, permissions, governance and arrangements for generating returns need to be examined carefully for each proposed venture.

For a British independent school, this means that selecting the right partner is not simply a question of finding a developer with sufficient capital. It requires a clear understanding of responsibilities, control, educational standards, financial flows and the consequences if the relationship fails.

Nor should a large national market be mistaken for a single addressable market. Demand is concentrated geographically, and the economics of a premium school in Jakarta may differ considerably from those elsewhere.

My experience is that international expansion works best when market research, due diligence, a clearly defined proposition and an agreed investment roadmap come before the excitement of the deal.

The opportunity may be substantial. The challenge is to convert it into a viable school.

Never thought making a game could be this fun! 🎮

It started with a spontaneous decision to join the last Game Jam of the year, hosted by Apple Developer Academy @ UC, Jakarta, with participants from academies across Indonesia and Korea.

Since this was my first time making a game, I wanted to explore something I've always found interesting: logic-based puzzle games. I've always loved games that don't tell players exactly what to do. Instead, they encourage you to observe, explore, and figure things out on your own. The theme was “Compact”, which got us thinking: what if compact wasn't just about making things smaller, but about bringing disconnected things closer together?

That's where our idea started: a puzzle game where players move platforms and shift perspectives to connect fragmented paths. But we also wanted the game to tell a story. We ended up connecting the concept to a quarter-life crisis, that phase of life when you feel stuck, unsure where you're going, and have to find your own way forward. And since one of our teammates loves flowers, we explored their meanings and wove them into Mori's emotional journey throughout each chapter.

And that's how Mori-chan came to life. 🪻

For me, one of the most exciting parts was the concepting process. There's something satisfying about seeing random ideas that once existed only in your head turn into something you can actually play.

From brainstorming puzzle mechanics and watching Dina Septy Puspayani bring them to life through code, to seeing Mori's world take shape through illustrations and assets created by Rizki Fitriani, Noorfi Azizah Rahim, and Diana N.. Seeing Safa Auliya H turn Mori's narrative into an in-game experience made everything feel even more connected. As for me, I ended up doing a little bit of everything: concepting, keeping things on track, creating assets, experimenting with maps and chapters, and working on chapter endings.

It was so much fun seeing all those pieces come together. Of course, not everything worked on the first try. There were experiments, revisions, unexpected challenges, and moments of “Wait, why isn't this working?” 😭 And the funny part? We built the whole thing in around 10 days.

There's still so much we could improve, but seeing a random idea become a playable game was incredibly rewarding. This experience made me realize how much I enjoy the creative side of game development, especially when working with people who bring different skills and perspectives together.

So, here's Mori-chan, our little perspective-based puzzle adventure.
Bring the world closer. 💜

PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera Officially Launches ARMUS AIP, a Schema-Based Data and Artificial Intelligence Platform Built in Indonesia
Unifying organizational data for AI assistants and no-code applications

BANDUNG, Indonesia, November 8, 2026
PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera today officially announced ARMUS AIP (AI Platform), a computer program in the form of a data and artificial intelligence (AI) platform built by its in-house team in Bandung. ARMUS AIP unifies data from multiple systems into a single shared data model (schema) and turns it into dashboards, applications, and AI assistants without a major migration.

Development Journey
Development of ARMUS AIP was initiated by the in-house team in Bandung on March 10, 2026. On June 2, 2026, the product underwent closed, limited functional testing by PT Algoritma Solusi Teknologi. Feedback from this testing was used to refine the platform before its official public announcement on November 8, 2026.

What ARMUS AIP Can Do
·       Unify data — from existing systems.
·       Shared data model — a schema understood the same way by every team.
·       Discover insights — explore and visualize data, including on maps.
·       AI assistants — ask questions and automate routine work.
·       No-code applications — build dashboards and operational applications.
·       Governance — manage access rights and record every change.
The platform is designed for the maritime, transportation, and security sectors, as well as general organizational data management.

Company Statement
“We built ARMUS AIP so that organizations in Indonesia can make full use of their own data in a secure and controlled way. This platform is the work of our engineering team in Bandung,” said the management of PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera.

Copyright Ownership
ARMUS AIP is an original computer program developed by the in-house team of PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera since March 10, 2026. All copyrights in its source code, user interface design, and documentation are owned by PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera; third-party and open-source components remain subject to their respective licenses.
This press release constitutes the official public announcement of ARMUS AIP, published in Bandung on November 8, 2026 through the official LinkedIn channel of PT Digital Pilar Sejahtera.

The stakes of the Apple Developer Academy @ UC, Jakarta’s Very Disco Game Jam just got higher. What started as a small community interest now includes every Apple Developer Academy in Asia! Academies from Jakarta, Korea, Bali, and Tangerang had to show their best craft in creating the best game on Apple platforms. For two straight weeks, every second mattered, and we had no time to waste.

The theme for the Game Jam was “Compact,” and we could interpret it as uniquely as we wanted, whether through the mechanics, the delivery, or the word itself. My previous Game Jam experience was exhausting and even a bit traumatizing, not because I didn’t enjoy it, but because I was overwhelmed by how many things we had to experiment with in such a short time. This Game Jam had a longer time frame, so we decided, why not?

Our interpretation of “Compact” was highly influenced by our everyday commuting life in Indonesia. Most of us take the train every day, and we have no choice but to squeeze into a very compact space with a lot of people. Muhammad Ridwan Novriansyah, our UI Designer, was reminded of a childhood game about putting people onto a train (whose name we all forgot), and Anselma Evelyn Pramono, our artist, really loved the game “Is This Seat Taken?” for its art and elegance. So we thought, why not combine both?

Enter Geo Metro, an iOS game where we help Shaples commute safely and comfortably by sorting them into the correct trains. The goal is simple: guide Shaples to their train, race against time, and the more Shaples you get in, the more you win! For the Game Jam submission, we prepared five levels in Geo Metro, each with increasing difficulty. We kept it as simple as possible so everyone can enjoy Geo Metro anywhere, even on the train itself!

Geo Metro came to life thanks to exceptional individuals, the same team that created the Lekara app. I mainly designed the game and its stages and coded the Shaple interactions in the world. Anselma Evelyn Pramono created every visual asset in the game. Alexander Johan Pramudito programmed the UI and connected the data. Ady Firdaus built the logic for the game stages. Alden Luthfi composed the wonderful jazz music you hear throughout the game. Muhammad Ridwan Novriansyah created the UI interactions and ambient sound effects, and he was also the one who inspired the game’s idea.

Geo Metro is certainly an improvement on what we had learned about game development, and although we didn’t take the top spot in the Game Jam, we enjoyed every moment of making it. 🇮🇩 INDONESIA JANGAN HANYA MENJADI PASAR AI!

Pasar kita besar. Tetapi, apakah kita mampu memenangkan nilai ekonominya?

Indonesia menghadapi pilihan: menjadi pemain dalam ekonomi AI, atau sekadar pasar bagi teknologi negara lain?

📊 1. PASAR BESAR, MONETISASI MENANTANG

Menurut PwC Indonesia (Juni 2026), pendapatan industri telekomunikasi Indonesia diperkirakan mencapai USD17–18 miliar pada 2025.

Namun, sekitar 97% pelanggan masih menggunakan layanan prepaid. Kompetisi harga dan tekanan ARPU menjadi tantangan struktural.

Pertumbuhan konsumsi data tidak otomatis menghasilkan nilai ekonomi yang sebanding.

📊 2. POSISI INDONESIA DI APAC

• Investasi AI: Menurut OECD, pada 2015–2024, investasi venture capital AI di ASEAN mencapai USD12,7 miliar di Singapura dan USD1,6 miliar di Indonesia. Hampir 8 kali lebih besar.

• Data center: Menurut Cushman & Wakefield, pipeline APAC mencapai 19,4 GW pada 2025. Greater Jakarta memiliki kapasitas operasional 322 MW. Kapasitas dalam konstruksi: Jakarta 186 MW vs Johor 315 MW. Dalam perencanaan: Jakarta 901 MW vs Johor 2.099 MW.

• Nilai ekonomi mobile: GSMA memperkirakan sektor mobile APAC menghasilkan USD1 triliun pada 2025 dan berpotensi mencapai USD1,4 triliun pada 2030.

Peluangnya besar, tetapi kompetisi regional bergerak cepat.

📊 3. DI MANA INDONESIA HARUS MENANG?

Lima area strategis:

1. Digital Infrastructure: fiber, 5G, data center, dan cloud.
2. AI Computing: GPU, AI platform, dan sovereign cloud.
3. Enterprise AI: solusi produktivitas bagi industri dan UMKM.
4. Digital Household: smart home, security, dan connected devices.
5. Local Ecosystem: startup, talenta, developer, dan intellectual property.

📊 4. APA YANG HARUS BERUBAH?

Transformasi Telco menjadi TechCo bukan sekadar mengganti nama atau menambah produk digital.

Yang dibutuhkan:
• Dari connectivity provider menjadi digital ecosystem orchestrator.
• Dari menjual bandwidth menjadi menawarkan solusi.
• Dari product-centric menjadi customer problem-centric.
• Dari mengejar trafik menjadi meningkatkan revenue, margin, dan customer lifetime value.
• Dari belanja teknologi menjadi penciptaan nilai ekonomi terukur.

Investasi AI harus disiplin: berbasis demand, energi, utilisasi, talenta, dan ROI.

🚀 PENUTUP

Indonesia punya pasar, pelanggan, jaringan, dan potensi besar. Namun, skala pasar bukan jaminan keunggulan kompetitif.

Kita tidak harus menciptakan semua teknologi sendiri. Tetapi kita harus membangun kapabilitas, ekosistem, dan model bisnis agar nilai tambah ekonomi tercipta di Indonesia.

INDONESIA TIDAK CUKUP HANYA MENJADI AI-READY NATION. KITA HARUS MENJADI AI VALUE-CREATING NATION.

Pemenang ekonomi AI bukan hanya yang paling banyak menggunakan teknologi, melainkan yang paling mampu mengubahnya menjadi nilai ekonomi.

Pertanyaannya: apakah Indonesia siap menjadi pemain, atau kembali menjadi pasar bagi pertumbuhan ekonomi digital negara lain?

My sincere thanks to the StratComs Events team for bringing people together at APNE 2026 in Macau—and especially to Christina Logan for inviting me back for the second time- I'm honored.

Events like this are valuable for more than the sessions. They create the chance to make new friends from around the world, exchange knowledge, and learn from experts across the industry. I was also privileged to present Indonesia’s opportunity at the intersection of nuclear energy, AI, and data centers.

In my presentation, “The Nuclear-AI Nexus: Powering the Future of Data Centers,” I focused on a timely question: how can Indonesia provide the reliable power needed for rapidly growing AI and data center demand?

Indonesia’s data center sector is expanding quickly, while much of its connected capacity remains concentrated in the Java-Madura-Bali system. That creates a strong case for data center developers to think seriously about bring your own power (BYOP)—including the generation, transmission, and interconnection needed to support their facilities.

This is a significant opportunity for nuclear energy. It can provide firm, low-carbon power for high-availability computing, and Indonesia’s nuclear ambitions are growing: from planned capacity in the near term toward around 35 GW by 2060. The opportunity extends beyond selling electricity to the national grid. Industrial estates, mining operations, and dedicated AI campuses could also become potential customers through direct commercial arrangements.

Indonesia is working toward a technology-neutral regulatory framework, and its licensing costs may be competitive with those in more established nuclear markets. Together with the scale of the data center buildout, this creates an opening to align nuclear development with customers who need dependable power and can support long-term investment.

Thank you again to Christina, the StratCom team, and everyone at APNE 2026 for the warm welcome and thoughtful conversations. I left Macau with new connections, fresh insights, and real optimism about the opportunities ahead.

posts.text:
Target 3,49jt lapangan kerja baru di 2027, tapi porsi kerja formalnya cuman 40%-an.

Artinya hampir 60% pekerja kita masih di sektor informal. Sedihnya, sekarang banyak banget talent berkualitas yang malah kerja informal. No disrespect, but it’s a shame.

Good thing now some of them have a chance. Through EOR, senior engineer atau marketer di Indonesia bisa digaji perusahaan luar pakai standar gaji di sana, sambil tetap kerja dari Indo dengan gaji dollar (klise, I know).

I don’t believe in work family, but I do believe friendship outside of work exists. And in this economy, fair2an aja kalau ada yang ambil a better opportunity.

Jadi saingan lu buat dapetin senior talent sekarang termasuk perusahaan luar.

Buat local founders dan C-level yang lagi nyusun headcount plan 2027, tiga hal yang perlu dibenerin dari sekarang:
1. Benchmark gaji role senior lu ke market yang sebenarnya, termasuk offer remote dari luar.
2. Tulis policy flexibility yang jelas di offer letter, jangan cuma janji pas interview.
3. Kasih career path dan struktur management yang kelihatan dari hari pertama.

Talent lokal kita world-class. Yang perlu di-upgrade itu cara kita nge-hire dan nge-retain mereka.

Agree to disagree is totally fine, drop prediksi lu soal job market 2027 di komen. Dan kalau lu lagi planning hiring senior buat 2027, DM me and see what we can work on.

🌍 PERBEDAAN STANDAR DRAWING DI DUNIA: ISO, ANSI, DIN, JIS & ASME
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dalam dunia Engineering Design dan Manufacturing, gambar teknik (Engineering Drawing) merupakan bahasa universal yang menjadi dasar komunikasi antara designer, engineer, dan manufacturer.
Namun, tahukah Anda bahwa setiap negara dan industri memiliki standar gambar teknik yang berbeda?
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Berikut 5 standar gambar teknik yang paling banyak digunakan di dunia :
🔹 1. ISO (International Organization for Standardization)
Standar internasional yang digunakan secara global. Umumnya menggunakan satuan metrik (mm) dan menjadi acuan dalam berbagai industri manufaktur.
🔹 2. ANSI (American National Standards Institute)
Standar yang banyak digunakan di Amerika Serikat. Mengatur format gambar teknik, simbol, dimensi, dan berbagai ketentuan engineering.
🔹 3. DIN (Deutsches Institut für Normung)
Standar asal Jerman yang dikenal dengan ketelitian, sistematis, dan penerapannya dalam industri engineering serta manufacturing di Eropa.
🔹 4. JIS (Japanese Industrial Standards)
Standar industri Jepang yang banyak diterapkan dalam industri otomotif, machinery, dan precision manufacturing.
🔹 5. ASME (American Society of Mechanical Engineers)
Standar yang sangat penting dalam mechanical engineering, khususnya untuk dimensioning, tolerancing, dan Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T)
------------------------------------------------------------
📌 APA YANG MEMBEDAKAN STANDAR TERSEBUT?
Beberapa aspek utama yang perlu diperhatikan:
🔸Satuan pengukuran (Metric & Imperial).
🔸Sistem toleransi dan dimensional accuracy.
🔸Simbol serta notasi gambar teknik.
🔸Jenis garis dan aturan penyajian gambar.
🔸Metode dimensioning dan GD&T.
🔸Regulasi serta kebutuhan industri masing-masing negara
------------------------------------------------------------------
💡 KESIMPULAN
Memahami perbedaan standar gambar teknik bukan hanya tentang membaca drawing, tetapi juga memastikan bahwa desain dapat diproduksi dengan benar, mengurangi kesalahan interpretasi, dan memenuhi persyaratan kualitas manufaktur.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

“Tambahin AI deh!” 

Kalimat yang sering didengar product manager dari atasan bahkan dari investor. Masalahnya, jarang ada yang lanjut bertanya: “AI untuk menyelesaikan masalah apa?”

Akhirnya banyak tim langsung lompat ke solusi. Pasang chatbot, tambah fitur “smart”, lalu bingung kenapa user tidak memakainya.

We’ve trained 1000+ product professionals from Gojek to Visa, polanya selalu sama. Fitur AI yang berhasil hampir tidak pernah berangkat dari teknologinya. Ia berangkat dari masalah user yang jelas.

Urutan yang kami paparkan cukup simple:

1️⃣ Petakan pain point user. Di mana mereka buang waktu, bingung, atau menyerah?
2️⃣ Baru tanyakan: apakah AI memang cara terbaik untuk menyelesaikannya? (Kadang tidak, dan itu tidak apa-apa.)
3️⃣ Uji dulu dengan prototype sederhana, bahkan tanpa coding, sebelum minta waktu engineer.
4️⃣ Tentukan metric sukses dan pikirkan soal kepercayaan user sejak awal.

Kamu gak perlu technical background untuk memimpin fitur AI. Yang kamu perlu adalah cara berpikir produk yang tepat dan self confidence untuk bicara dengan tim data dan engineering.

Ekosistem digital Indonesia tumbuh sangat cepat. PM yang bisa membawa AI ke produk dengan benar, bukan sekadar ikut tren, akan sangat dicari.

Kalau boleh tau, gimana saat ini tim kamu menerapkan AI? 

For more info: https://colabcohorts.com

Vendor Anda di luar negeri dan jadwal FAT sudah dekat. Siapa yang akan mewakili perusahaan Anda di pabrik?

Misalnya, equipment Anda sedang dibuat di China dan FAT dijadwalkan minggu depan. Engineer QA/QC yang biasa menangani equipment tersebut berhalangan hadir atau mungkin anda bahkan tidak punya tim QAQC yang memiliki kapabilitas yang mumpuni. Akhirnya muncul opsi, 

“Siapa yang bisa berangkat minggu depan?”

Jangan asal kirim orang cuma karena dia yang available. Saat FAT, orang yang hadir perlu paham equipment-nya, tahu apa yang perlu dicek, berpengalaman, dan bisa menyampaikan ke tim Anda kalau ada hasil pengujian yang perlu ditindaklanjuti.

Lewat Vendor Surveillance Services (VSS), kami di Applus+ Indonesia bisa bantu menyediakan third-party inspector yang kualifikasi dan pengalamannya sesuai dengan jenis equipment serta scope proyek Anda.

Applus memiliki jaringan yang mencakup lebih dari 5.000 inspektor lapangan yang sudah melalui asesmen di 69 negara, termasuk China, Korea Selatan, Jepang, Amerika Serikat, dan berbagai negara di Eropa.
Dukungan ini bisa digunakan untuk proyek di sektor oil & gas, power, renewables, construction, dan mining, antara lain untuk:

🔹 Factory Acceptance Test (FAT)
Inspektor hadir di fasilitas vendor untuk menyaksikan pengujian sebelum equipment dikirim. Hasil dan temuan dicatat sesuai Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) supaya tim Anda bisa review dan follow up dengan vendor selagi equipment masih di pabrik.

🔹 Site Acceptance Test (SAT)
Setelah equipment terpasang di lokasi proyek, inspektor bisa menyaksikan pengujian untuk memverifikasi fungsinya sesuai kriteria penerimaan yang disepakati.
Kalau perlu mulai lebih awal, kami juga bisa bantu inspeksi selama fabrikasi, review dokumen kualitas, expediting, hingga pre-shipment inspection.

posts.text:
Touching Grass, Talking Cloud!

Had a great time at Amazon Web Services (AWS) Community Day Jakarta 2026 last week! Lots of interesting sessions and insightful conversations.

As an AI Engineer, I spend most of my time working on models and applications, so getting to explore the infrastructure and platform side of things was a nice change of pace (and a reminder of how much I still don't know).

I got to learn about what goes on behind the scenes when running LLMs on Amazon EKS, from model serving and GPU autoscaling with Karpenter to fine-tuning workflows with Kubeflow. It was also interesting to see how small ML model can be used for autonomous K8s right-sizing and optimizing infrastructure costs. Apparently, ML isn't just creating infrastructure headaches, it can help solve them too.

Another part I enjoyed was hearing directly from experienced industry leaders: Arief N., Doddy Kristianto, Adrianus B. Kurnadi, Ts. Shah Hassan about cloud and career. It's refreshing to hear perspectives from people who've spent years building things, making decisions, and learning from what didn't go as planned.

And of course, the conversations outside the sessions were just as valuable. I got to talk with other engineers and students, and it was interesting how people at different stages of their careers could bring completely different perspectives to the same problem.

As engineers, we spend so much time behind our keyboards that it's easy to get comfortable with our own ways of thinking. Sometimes, a simple conversation with someone outside our usual circle can challenge assumptions we didn't even realize we had.

Definitely a good reason to close the IDE and touch some grass (while still talking about tech).

Huge thanks to AWS User Group Indonesia, the speakers, organizers, and everyone I got to chat with!

The ASEAN Summit will last only a few days. Its economic impact should last for years.
As the Philippines prepares for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, I find myself looking at it not only as a Filipino, but as someone who has spent more than 25 years in manufacturing and engineering. 
We have a tremendous opportunity.
But hosting world leaders is one thing. Convincing companies to build their next factory, engineering center, or supply chain here is another.
Can we turn ASEAN leadership into manufacturing investment, stronger industries, and better jobs for Filipinos?
The Philippines has talent. We have experienced engineers, manufacturing professionals, a strong electronics sector, and decades of experience supporting multinational operations.
What we need is an ecosystem that turns those strengths into investment.
Reliable and competitive energy.
Efficient logistics.
Stronger local suppliers.
Industry-ready technical skills.
Smart automation.
Faster industrial development.
Because our competition is not standing still.
Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and other ASEAN economies are competing for many of the same investments and jobs.
So when the summit ends and the delegates leave, I hope we ask a different question:
What did ASEAN create for the Filipino worker, engineer, manufacturer, and entrepreneur?
Did we attract investment?
Did we strengthen local suppliers?
Did we create better engineering and manufacturing jobs?
Did we make Philippine manufacturing more competitive?
For me, hosting ASEAN is an honor, successful hosting is good.
Turning regional visibility into industrial competitiveness, investment, technology, and better-paying jobs is even better.
That is the ASEAN legacy I would like to see.

#ASEAN2026 #Philippines #Manufacturing #PhilippineEconomy #EngineeringLeadership #Industrialization #SupplyChain #FutureOfManufacturing

posts.text:
Procurement Acceptance Criteria for Painting Lines: 10–20 Installations, 5–10 Years Zero Shutdowns

Acceptance criteria decide whether a painting line becomes a production asset or a maintenance liability. Yet most procurement documents still describe intentions — uniform coating, low maintenance, stable operation — and suppliers answer with adjectives. The practical fix is mechanical: every condition gets a number, a measurement method, and a reference project where that number was actually held.

Four performance figures that belong in the contract

Coating yield. A 20-line automotive parts programme running in Germany, Russia, Thailand, Indonesia, Mexico and China reports 98% coating yield on structural parts, chassis components and interior trim. A 20-line cookware programme in Russia, Iran, India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Thailand and China reports 98% coating uniformity across multi-size pans, pots and baking trays.

Consumption per part. On the automotive lines, paint consumption fell 25% and energy 20%. Cookware and wood furniture programmes report 30% lower paint consumption; a 15-line metal coating programme reports 30% lower paint/powder consumption and 22% lower energy.

Coating performance and pass rate. Ten complete industrial equipment lines serving construction machinery, agricultural equipment and rail transit components hold anti-corrosion performance to ≥1000-hour salt spray testing, with a 98% pass rate. The metal programme reports 97%.

Uptime. Five to ten years of stable continuous operation with zero major shutdowns was recorded on the automotive and metal programmes. The wood furniture programme reports zero major quality complaints over the same period, alongside a 90% reduction in dust defects and 40% higher production efficiency.

Three rules for wording the criteria

First, fix the part family and the mix before fixing the number. A yield figure earned on one reference part says little about a mixed-model schedule.

Second, fix the measurement method and the production baseline before signature. Consumption savings only exist relative to a stated film thickness and a stated paint. A 100% pre-shipment test is a usable release gate; a minimum order quantity of two units makes a small validation batch commercially realistic.

Third, define the words that trigger claims. "Shutdown", "major defect" and "response time" should carry thresholds in writing, matched to the service terms being offered — remote technical support, a one-year warranty and a four-hour response commitment mean different things without a clock attached.

What has to sit behind the number

Intelligent monitoring, low-maintenance design, controlled coating thickness and adaptability to mixed production are the mechanisms that make a yield figure repeatable rather than a good month. Attractivechina (Guangdong Chuangzhi Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd.) builds these lines at a 35,548 m² site in Zhaoqing with a 54-engineer R&D team and 300-plus patents, which is the kind of detail worth requesting as a validation route rather than a credential.

Where installation count stops being evidence

Twenty lines across six countries proves the engineering has met different part families and different compliance environments. It does not prove your line will hit your number. A reference list becomes evidence only when your acceptance test is written against your parts, your film thickness and your measurement method — and when the same method is applied during factory acceptance, installation and the first production month.

posts.text:
In intensively managed agricultural systems across Indonesia, we consistently observe a dramatic decline in earthworm populations—often ranging from 80% to 95%. This trend extends beyond an ecological issue; it signals a fundamental degradation of soil function that directly undermines crop productivity and farm sustainability.

Earthworms are critical ecosystem engineers. Their burrowing activity enhances soil aeration, improves water infiltration, and facilitates the integration of organic residues into the soil matrix. The loss of these biological conduits results in soil compaction, restricted root growth, and diminished nutrient availability—factors that collectively reduce crop resilience and yield potential.

The primary drivers behind this decline include excessive pesticide and herbicide application coupled with intensive tillage practices, which disrupt earthworm habitat and soil microbial communities. From a soil chemistry standpoint, recovery is optimized when soil pH is maintained near neutrality (approximately 7.5), organic carbon content is elevated (targeting around 20%), and the carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio is balanced near 18. Additionally, micronutrients such as iron, manganese, zinc, and copper are essential in sustaining microbial and faunal diversity, supporting broader soil biological functions.

To reverse earthworm population losses, farm management must prioritize reducing chemical inputs and minimizing soil disturbance. Incorporating organic amendments that provide stable carbon sources and maintain soil cation exchange capacity (KTK around 120 cmol(+)) is fundamental to rebuilding a biologically active soil environment. Vermicompost applications can serve as a practical intervention to reintroduce earthworm populations and accelerate improvements in soil structure and fertility.

From a strategic perspective, restoring earthworm activity should be integrated into broader soil health frameworks aimed at enhancing long-term system resilience and productivity. Monitoring biological indicators alongside chemical and physical soil parameters is essential to guide adaptive management.

How have you observed changes in earthworm populations on your farms? What specific management adjustments have yielded measurable improvements in soil biological activity?

I welcome your insights and am available to discuss tailored strategies relevant to your context.

A few months have passed since the completion of Package 5 and the end of my journey with the Project Management Unit (PMU) under the Ministry of Transportation of the Republic of Indonesia.

Looking back, I feel fortunate to have contributed to Patimban Port, one of Indonesia's National Strategic Projects, funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).

I joined in February 2023, just five months after graduating from university. It was a remarkable start to my career, stepping into a major port development project with a complex scope of works and a multinational environment, working alongside professionals from Japan, Indonesia, and other countries.

Along the way, I gained firsthand exposure to Japanese construction technologies, including Cement Deep Mixing (CDM) for ground improvement and Cement Pipe Mixing (CPM) for reclamation, as well as large scale dredging works to a design depth of −14.0 m LWS. I also learned about FIDIC based contract administration and had the opportunity to engage with experienced Dispute Board professionals.

From commencement through the completion milestone on 17 July 2026 and the subsequent handover process, there were many challenges and achievements along the way. One of the most memorable moments towards the end of my journey was witnessing the successful berthing trials at the Car Berth and Service Boat Berth, including the trial involving MOL's car carrier MV BLANCO ACE. Seeing the berths successfully accommodate vessels after years of construction was a rewarding way to conclude my time at Patimban.

I'm proud to have been part of this project and grateful to everyone I worked with across the Employer, Engineer, Contractor, and other stakeholders.

Patimban will always be an important part of where my career began. As I move into a new role spanning a wider range of projects and business activities, I look forward to building on what I've learned, adapting to new challenges, and continuing to grow.

posts.text:
Compliance Theater Is Not Cybersecurity

BLUF: One defensive line won’t hold in 2026-27. Split your architecture in two: a layer built to satisfy regulators and a layer built to defeat machines. Confusing them is how enterprises get breached or fined.

AI-assisted attacks now map perimeters and probe sandboxes at machine speed. For companies scaling across volatile G20 corridors, cross-border architecture needs two distinct layers.

1. The Surface Theater (compliance)
This layer is built for humans and regulators: Big Four readiness binders, pre-certified hyperscaler regions inside domestic borders, and steady government-to-government diplomacy. Together they keep FDI flowing, keep liability insurable, and satisfy localization text like Indonesia’s PP 33/2026. It’s necessary, but it’s a performance, not a defense.

2. The Infrastructure Bowels (AI-era armor)
Beneath it sits the unglamorous layer that assumes the perimeter is already compromised.

The key insight is that an AI model or cloud sandbox has document literacy but no situational awareness. It can’t see its own packets or know which country its disk sits in. Route cross-border data through a standard cloud API so a model can “audit” your files, and it will read them beautifully while breaching localization mandates. Under laws like Indonesia’s UU PDP, that means fines of up to 2% of global annual revenue.

The winning play: don’t over-engineer the surface, and don’t wait for a more compliant chatbot. Hardcode regional data boundaries and zero-trust outbound perimeters into the data plumbing from day one:

Stateless, inbound-blind ingestion gates and local cryptographic sidecars on domestic soilRaw citizen identifiers and primary records locked to domestic disks, under native jurisdictionOutbound buffers that stream only anonymous, irreversible telemetry hashes to the global data lake

This satisfies a state forensic audit in full and shrinks what an attacker can ever exfiltrate.

The compliance theater satisfies the lawyers. The infrastructure bowels defeat the machines.

Global capital should build a beautiful stage for the sky, while fortifying the physical gates to the ground.

#Cybersecurity #DataSovereignty #ZeroTrust #AI #Indonesia
